new_commits.author: xy200303
new_commits.message:
[Fix] Accept the safe-gate lower bound on the GDN-2 Ascend intra route

chunk_gdn2_fwd_intra passes lower_bound to every implementation, but the
Ascend verifier and chunk_gdn2_fwd_intra_npu spelled their parameters out
and never learned the argument. Backend.verify swallows the resulting
TypeError and reports the backend as inapplicable, so an NPU call with
safe_gate=True silently fell back to Triton instead of taking the Ascend
path.

The NPU kernel needs no offset from it: each of its blocks anchors on its
own first row, so the pairwise gate differences it exponentiates are
already non-positive for the safe-gate range.

new_commits.author: xy200303
new_commits.message:
[Test] Cover the GDN-2 backward and varlen prefix-causality anchors

The forward regression could not see the two anchors the backward intra
kernel carries: on (T, P) = (40, 33) the leak reached dg while the prefix
output alone stayed bit-identical. Add a backward case over three shapes
that checks the prefix output, dg, dA_log and ddt_bias, plus a varlen case
over two segmentations, where the anchor was previously T-relative and so
moved with the segment boundary.

The shared input and gate-flip helpers keep the three regressions on the
same tensors.

fresh_replies.body:
Fixed — `lower_bound` is now in both signatures (`8a20e054`). You are right about the mechanism: the verifier's `TypeError` is swallowed by `BaseBackend.verify`, so an NPU call with `safe_gate=True` was being reported as inapplicable and silently took the Triton path rather than the Ascend one.

The NPU kernel accepts the argument and ignores it on purpose, and I noted why in the code: every one of its blocks anchors on its own first row, so the pairwise gate differences it exponentiates are already non-positive across the safe-gate range and it needs no centring offset. The KDA Ascend verifiers spell their parameters as `*args, **kwargs`, which is why the same shape did not break there.

`fla/ops/gdn2/backends/triton_ascend/` matches the NPU CI pattern, so the A2 jobs on this push exercise this route.

Added in `df6759bd`.

`test_chunk_gdn2_prefix_causality_bwd` runs (22, 21), (40, 33) and (70, 69) and asserts bitwise equality of the prefix output, `dg`, `dA_log` and `ddt_bias`. (40, 33) is in there on purpose: that is the shape where the leak reached `dg` while the prefix output alone stayed identical, so a forward-only check could not have caught it.

`test_chunk_gdn2_prefix_causality_varlen` runs `[0, 8, 30]` and `[0, 22, 92]`, where the anchor used to be `T`-relative and so moved with the segment boundary. Every case ends a sequence inside a sub-chunk whose middle row is its last valid token, and the prefix spans the earlier segment in the varlen ones, so a leak has to cross the boundary to show up.

The three regressions now share their inputs and the gate-flip helper, so they run on the same tensors.

life update: I've recently left @Kimi_Moonshot!

The past year at Kimi has been the best of my life so far. I'm deeply grateful to have worked with and learned from such amazing and supportive colleagues.

Some of my favorite memories include (in chronological order): optimizing

fetch_manifest.scope: One known departure post only; syndication is not timeline coverage. Long-post text is a truncated preview.

pre_run_registration.note: Design registered before implementation. Final code and protocol frozen before tests/model comparisons. No imported experiment modules in this registration helper.

independent_static_review.scope: Read-only static source/test/protocol and installed implementation review. stdlib hash/AST only; no production imports, tests, Torch/model execution or network.

manual_review.actual_class_and_nested_scope: Actual GPTNeoXAttention isinstance selection; closure binds each original and record; nested hooks active only inside actual forward. Outer model and all thirteen actual LayerNorm policies preserved; six expected attention names and class checked.
manual_review.protected_parameters_and_exact_loss: Unchanged codec protects backing-storage parameter aliases before size/dtype eligibility. CE created after all hooks exit. Parameter hashes and complete finite gradients checked each arm; dense reference detached and cloned.
manual_review.baseline_parity_and_restoration: Dense and norm-only policies mathematically match prior treatment; tests require exact logits/loss/logits-gradient and every parameter-gradient hash. finally restores pre-existing raw instance forward or removes added attribute on success and exceptions.
manual_review.independent_vjp: NumPy float64 manual VJP has correct interleaved per-head QKV packing, causal row softmax derivative, dV=P^T dA, dQ=dS K/sqrtD, dK=dS^T Q/sqrtD, both linear weight/bias and input derivatives. Identity RoPE and zero dropout explicitly restrict this independent reference.
manual_review.fixed_design_and_gate: Three fixed first batches, no optimizer or holdout, CPU float32 eager, fresh workers and time caps. Ratio gate fails on invalid/nonpositive baseline, negative/nonfinite treatment or nonfinite ratio/cosines; requires <=0.5 and cosine no worse all seeds.
manual_review.limits: Broad attention-forward scope includes projections/RoPE and does not isolate an operand or prove training quality, efficiency, peak memory, AttnRes or novelty. Overlapping synthetic batches are not independent replicates.

independent_result_review.scope: Independent stdlib-only retained raw-worker/report/hash/metric arithmetic, actual save-scope inventory and exact full prior-norm baseline record audit. No production imports, tests, Torch/model execution or gradient array regeneration. Reported finite gradient coverage is checked against raw records, not independently regenerated arrays.
